prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Miami for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every Miami car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, whether the case will likely settle or go to trial, your language and communication preferences, and how you want the firm to handle medical liens and negotiations.

How to find the best lawyer for your case
- Look for experience with car-accidents and serious-injury claims (not just pass-through referrals). Ask how many similar cases they’ve handled and their trial experience.  
- Track record: ask about representative settlements/verdicts (not just advertising claims).  
- Resources: big insurers require firms that can front medical lien costs and expert fees.  
- Communication: how often will you get updates, who is your point of contact, and how accessible is the lawyer?  
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no up-front fee). Ask the percentage, when it increases, and what expenses you may owe if you don’t recover.  
- Client reviews and professional recognition: check Google/Yelp, Martindale-Hubbell, Super Lawyers, Avvo/National Trial Lawyers, and any Florida Bar discipline history.  
- Local reputation: Miami-Dade legal community and trial experience in local courts matters.

Practical checks and questions for a free consult
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled? How many went to trial?  
- What is a realistic settlement range given my injuries?  
- Who will handle my case day-to-day?  
- What contingency fee and costs should I expect?  
- How do you handle medical liens and past/future medical expenses?  
- Can you provide references from recent clients?

Useful resources to find and vet Miami lawyers
- Florida Bar Lawyer Referral Service / Attorney Search (to verify bar status and discipline)  
- Super Lawyers (Florida/Miami list)  
- Martindale-Hubbell peer-review ratings  
- Local firms’ client reviews (Google/Yelp/BBB)  
- Miami-Dade Trial Lawyers Association / National Trial Lawyers lists

Important deadlines and documents
- Florida statute of limitations for most personal injury car-accident claims is generally 4 years from the crash date — confirm immediately to avoid losing rights.  
- Bring: police report, photos of scene/vehicles/injuries, medical records and bills, insurance info (yours and the other driver’s), wage-loss documentation, and any witness contact info.

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short vetted list of highly rated Miami car-accident attorneys (I’ll search Super Lawyers, Martindale, Google reviews, and firm trial results) — tell me your ZIP or neighborhood, severity of injuries, and whether you prefer Spanish/English.  
- Or draft a set of questions you can use during consultations.

Which would you prefer?
